# Resources reference

Every class in `assets/scripts/resources/`, from its doc comments. The overview is in [README.md](README.md).

- [InputActionsRes](#inputactionsres)
- [PawnDefaultsRes](#pawndefaultsres)
- [TagDeclarationsRes](#tagdeclarationsres)

## InputActionsRes

`res://assets/scripts/resources/InputActions_resource.gd`, extends [`Resource`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_resource.html)

The list of named actions a game uses, such as jump, sprint and primary.

Pawn spec section 5. InputActions reads this (resources/input_actions.tres), and gives each action a bit in the order it's listed, so every machine in a multiplayer game agrees on them.

To add an action, add its name to the end of the list. Adding it in the middle works too, but it moves the bits of everything after it, which only matters if something saved a bit mask to a file.

### Settings and properties

- `actions: StringName[]` = `[]`: One name per action. Players press these through the key map on PlayerController, and AI presses them through AIController.

## PawnDefaultsRes

`res://assets/scripts/resources/PawnDefaults_resource.gd`, extends [`Resource`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_resource.html)

The parts every pawn gets unless its own scene already has one of the same name, and other game-wide pawn settings.

PawnInitializer reads this (pawn spec section 11). One file per game (resources/pawn_defaults.tres), so a designer changes every pawn's defaults in one place.

Each part is a small scene, so its settings can be changed in the editor. A part's name is its scene's root node name, and a pawn that has a child with that name keeps its own. Parts are added in this list's order, the same on every machine.

### Settings and properties

- `parts: PackedScene[]` = `[]`: The default parts, in the order they're added.
- `ai_brain: PackedScene`: The AI brain a pawn gets when its own scene has none: an AIBehaviourManager scene with its behaviours as children (a behaviour set the manager scores and picks between, not a behaviour tree). Used instead of the parts list's behaviour-less one, and a player's pawn gets it too: its AI waits while a player has it and takes over when they let go. Empty: the parts list's.
- `world_load_distance: float` = `320.0`: How far a pawn that keeps the world loaded (a player's, or one whose PawnStreamingSource has keeps_world_loaded on) loads ground around it, in metres.
- `world_nav_distance: float` = `128.0`: How far nav is built around such a pawn, in metres. Building nav as far out as the ground would be slow (about 100 tiles a chunk), so it's shorter. 0 builds none. It can't exceed world_load_distance.

## TagDeclarationsRes

`res://assets/scripts/resources/TagDeclarations_resource.gd`, extends [`Resource`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_resource.html)

A list of tags a game declares up front, for one tag set.

Each tag set reads its own file at startup and gives bits in sorted order, so every machine in a multiplayer game agrees on them: TagRegistry (ability categories, tag_declarations.tres), NavTags (nav_tag_declarations.tres) and EffectTags (effect_tag_declarations.tres). Write full names with dots for levels ("combat.melee.sword"); parent levels ("combat", "combat.melee") are added automatically.

### Settings and properties

- `tags: StringName[]` = `[]`: The tags, full names with dots.
